name: Lyu Dalong
current_role: Non-executive director, OmniVision Integrated Circuits Group (formerly Will Semiconductor, 603501.SH); founding partner & co-chairman, Qingkong Yinxing (TusHoldings Ginkgo) venture capital
profile: Born 1962, a 1978-entry Tsinghua thermal-engineering graduate who worked as an Air Force engineering-design engineer (1983-92) before turning to investment. Through Beijing Huaqing vehicles (incl. Beijing Huaqing OmniVision Technology) he backed Will Semi's 2019 acquisition of OmniVision image sensors; he runs Tsinghua-linked VC firms Qingkong Yinxing and Ginkgo Angel Investment Center.
interesting_fact: Nominated in May 2025 to the board of Will Semi as it renamed itself OmniVision Group - one of China's largest CMOS image-sensor designers, supplying smartphone and automotive cameras.
deep_cut_fact: Tsinghua named a building after him: the 'Lyu Dalong Building' (southeast building of the Ziqiang S&T complex), a gift he and his wife He Shan made for Tsinghua's 110th anniversary, opened on 8 April 2024. He also funds young humanities faculty (2025) and an alumni lifelong-learning program.
notes: Low public profile; best known in Tsinghua alumni/VC circles. Route via OmniVision board office (board secretary Ren Bing, tel +86 21 50805043) or Qingkong Yinxing. 2025 filing says he held no shares directly - stake is indirect via Huaqing entities.

name: Binaben Nimish Chudgar
current_role: Chudgar family shareholder in Intas Pharmaceuticals (Ahmedabad); no public executive role found
profile: Listed by Hurun India (2018-2019) as a wealth holder through Intas Pharmaceuticals, the Ahmedabad generics and biosimilars maker founded by Hasmukh Chudgar and run by his sons Binish, Nimish and Urmish. The name format indicates she is linked to Nimish Chudgar (Intas joint MD), but no public source describing her could be found.
interesting_fact: Intas, the family's company, is one of India's largest privately held drugmakers and owns UK/EU generics arm Accord Healthcare.
notes: Very private; no profile, interviews or roles found under 'Binaben'/'Bina' Chudgar. Relationship to Nimish Chudgar inferred only from name format - unverified. Only route is Intas corporate office (general queries).

name: Liu Peiying
current_role: No public role found; listed by Hurun China (2010-2014) jointly with China Dongxiang chairman Chen Yihong
profile: Appeared on the Hurun China Rich List 2010-2014 as a co-holder (with Chen Yihong) of the fortune derived from China Dongxiang (3818.HK), the Beijing sportswear group that holds the Kappa brand in mainland China and Macau. Her exact relationship to Chen Yihong is not confirmed in any source found, and she does not appear in recent HKEX disclosure-of-interest filings.
interesting_fact: China Dongxiang owns all rights to the Italian Kappa brand in mainland China, and in 2008 bought Japan's Phenix Co., which managed Kappa and Phenix in Japan, to push into ski and outdoor fashion.
notes: No public profile; 2026 HKEX circular names the Chen family group (Chen Yihong, daughter Chen Chen, her spouse, brother Chen Yiyong) but not Liu Peiying. Likely a family member of Chen Yihong (unconfirmed). Only route is China Dongxiang IR. Off Hurun list since 2014.

name: Lyu Gang
current_role: Chairman and general manager, Zhejiang Jingxin Pharmaceutical (002020.SZ; Hong Kong H-share listing filed Sept 2026)
profile: Born 1962, Lyu Gang has run Zhejiang Jingxin Pharmaceutical, a Xinchang-born drugmaker now based in Hangzhou, since its days as Zhejiang Xinchang Jingxin Pharma; he has been chairman since 2004 when it listed in Shenzhen. With his wife he controls ~36% of the company, which focuses on CNS and cardio/cerebrovascular drugs (2025 revenue RMB4.07bn) and is seeking a second listing in Hong Kong.
interesting_fact: Jingxin's only approved innovative drug is the insomnia treatment dimdazenil (Jingnuoning); it is also developing JX2201 for elevated lipoprotein(a), and is pursuing an HKEX dual listing with CITIC Securities as sole sponsor.
deep_cut_fact: His formal education started with a mechanical-engineering associate degree from Zhejiang Radio & TV University (1987); he later did Peking University Guanghua's EMBA (2000) and a China Pharmaceutical University pharmacy certificate (2004), and earned senior-economist title in Dec 2022.
notes: Board secretary Hong Yunfei (tel 0571-86575888) is the published IR route. Company is mid-way through a Hong Kong IPO (refiled Sept 2026), so may be in a quiet period.

name: Scott D. Ferguson
current_role: Founder, Managing Partner & Portfolio Manager, Sachem Head Capital Management (NYC activist hedge fund); director, Performance Food Group; Delivery Hero supervisory board
profile: Activist investor who founded Sachem Head in 2012 after nine years at Bill Ackman's Pershing Square, which he joined at its 2003 inception. Sachem Head runs concentrated value/activist campaigns (past boards: Autodesk, Olin, Elanco, US Foods). He joined PFG's board in Sept 2025 under a cooperation deal while pushing a US Foods combination; a Sachem Head partner sits on Six Flags' board.
interesting_fact: Before investing he was a McKinsey business analyst (1996-99) and VP at private-equity firm American Industrial Partners (1999-2001); he holds a Stanford A.B. in Public Policy and a 2003 Harvard MBA.
deep_cut_fact: He was at Pershing Square from day one (2003) - joining Ackman straight out of Harvard Business School - and outside finance serves on the boards of Henry Street Settlement and the Robin Hood Foundation.

public_contacts.value: Longacre Square Partners (Dan Zacchei / Joe Germani) - Sachem@Longacresquare.com

notes: SEC 'director' flag for Six Flags (FUN) likely reflects Sachem Head's board designee Jonathan Brudnick (appointed Oct 2025), not Ferguson personally. Twilio stake is from Sachem Head's fund. Longacre Square is the best media route.

name: Zhang Weiming
current_role: Chairman, Shanghai Shengjian Technology (603324.SH; formerly Shengjian Environment, renamed Aug 2024)
profile: Co-founder (with Wang Zhe) and chairman of Shanghai-based Shengjian, which supplies process-exhaust-gas treatment systems to China's semiconductor and display fabs. It grew from making a single exhaust-duct product into a full system integrator, listed on the SSE main board in April 2021, and is now pushing upstream into semiconductor equipment and materials.
interesting_fact: Shengjian dominated the niche of fab exhaust ductwork before 2011, then rode BOE-led domestic display-panel build-outs into full waste-gas treatment systems; Zhang's motto is to 'take the hardest road' and build a 'hundred-year company'.
deep_cut_fact: In its start-up years Shengjian's stainless-steel coated exhaust duct won FM Approvals certification for cleanroom exhaust/smoke duct systems; Zhang compares the climb upmarket to mountaineering: 'the higher you go, the fewer companions, the more beautiful the view.'
notes: Re-elected chairman 2024. Highly relevant to semiconductor-fab infrastructure angle. IR route is the board office.

name: Liu Haibin
current_role: Major individual shareholder (~62m shares, among top-3 holders) of Shanghai Bairun Investment Holding Group (002568.SZ, RIO cocktails); no current executive role found
profile: Early partner of Bairun founder Liu Xiaodong. Bairun began in 1997 as a Shanghai flavours-and-fragrances maker; Liu Haibin held a large stake in it and about 24% of its spun-out alcopop unit Shanghai Bacchus (maker of RIO), which Bairun re-acquired via share issuance in 2015. He and his wife Ma Xiaohua remain top shareholders of the group, which dominates China's ready-to-drink cocktail market and is moving into whisky.
interesting_fact: RIO, the brand behind his fortune, held close to 90% of China's pre-mixed cocktail market by 2021; Bairun still runs its original flavours business under the Bairun name.
notes: Very low profile; no interviews found. 2025 annual report lists him as a top-10 holder (62.16m shares) and confirms he and Ma Xiaohua are spouses. Route only via Bairun board office.

name: Xiao Zhengqiang
current_role: Chairman and co-actual controller, Luoyang Xinqianglian Slewing Bearing (300850.SZ, ChiNext)
profile: Born 1971 in Henan, Xiao Zhengqiang and his brother Xiao Gaoqiang (general manager) built Luoyang Xinqianglian into a maker of large slewing bearings, wind-turbine main-shaft bearings and tunnel-boring-machine bearings, supplying wind OEMs such as Mingyang and Envision. Listed on ChiNext in 2020; he has been chairman since 2016.
interesting_fact: Xinqianglian's growth came from localising large wind-turbine main-shaft bearings, long dominated by foreign suppliers, as Chinese wind OEMs pushed domestic sourcing.
deep_cut_fact: Before bearings, he spent 13 years (1992-2005) as deputy head then head of the expatriate camp of French contractor Dumez on Lot 3 of the Xiaolangdi Dam on the Yellow River, after starting as a purchasing supervisor for the Xiaolangdi services company in 1990. He has a high-school education.
notes: Strong fit for energy (wind) angle. Route via board secretary Kou Congmei's office.

name: Qiao Yuhua
current_role: Actual controller and director, Inner Mongolia Shuangxin Environment-Friendly Material (001369.SZ, listed Dec 2025); chairman, Shuangxin Resources
profile: Born 1966, an accountant by training who rose from cement/iron plant bookkeeper in Qipanjing (Otog Banner, Ordos) to found the Shuangxin chemical group in 2000. Shuangxin turns calcium carbide into polyvinyl alcohol (PVA) and derivatives used in construction, paper, fibres, PVB film and water-soluble film; he controls ~62% of the voting rights of the SZSE-listed unit.
interesting_fact: Shuangxin listed on the Shenzhen main board in late 2025 and is using IPO funds to move downstream from PVA into PVB (laminated-glass interlayer) and VAE emulsion products.
deep_cut_fact: His first job (1986) was at the Qipanjing cement & iron plant; he then worked four years at the ICBC Qipanjing office in Otog Banner before returning to the plant as finance chief - he holds an accounting degree from the Central Institute of Finance and is a senior engineer.
notes: Energy-intensive coal-chemical business in Ordos (carbide, captive power) - relevant to energy angle. Low media profile; route via board office of Shuangxin Materials.

name: Chen Weilin
current_role: No current public role found; formerly chairman & GM of Xinjiang TBEA Group (TBEA's controlling shareholder) and a director of TBEA Co. (600089.SH)
profile: A Xinjiang TBEA veteran (born c.1959) who served as chairman and general manager of Xinjiang TBEA Group Co., the holding company that controls Urumqi-based transformer, cable, polysilicon and power-project giant TBEA, and sat on TBEA's listed board around 2010-2012. His Hurun listing (2009-2022) reflects his stake in the TBEA holding structure; by 2016 Hu Shujun had replaced him as the group's legal representative.
interesting_fact: TBEA, whose holding company he chaired, is - alongside TWBB and XD Group - one of China's major transformer makers, and also builds transmission and renewable-energy projects (with a manufacturing base in Gujarat, India).
notes: Role confirmed from TBEA 2010-2011 annual reports (https://static.cninfo.com.cn/finalpage/2011-03-31/59206475.PDF). No longer in TBEA's 2016+ filings; current activities unknown. Very low profile; TBEA securities office is the only published route. Strong fit for grid/energy angle.

name: Zhu Muzhi
current_role: Unknown - no public record found under the name 朱沐之; Hurun (2014-2021) ties the fortune to Guangdong Xin Nanfang (New South) Group
profile: Hurun China listed Zhu Muzhi 2014-2021 for Xin Nanfang Group, the Guangzhou real-estate and traditional-Chinese-medicine conglomerate. Public sources name Zhu Layi (elder brother of Hopson founder Zhu Mengyi) as Xin Nanfang's founder (1994); no source links the name 朱沐之 to the group, so this may be an alias, alternate name or family member - unverified.
interesting_fact: Xin Nanfang, the group behind this listing, pivoted early from property into TCM, investing for over a decade in artemisinin anti-malaria projects across Africa with Prof. Li Guoqiao, and backs Deng Lao herbal tea.
notes: Identity unresolved: zero search hits for 朱沐之. If the journalist means Xin Nanfang's founder, that is Zhu Layi (a former barefoot doctor and Guangzhou TCM College graduate). Do not use facts here for outreach without confirming the person.

name: James E. Douglas III
current_role: Private investor; member of the Douglas family investor group (led by IMAX director Kevin Douglas) that owns ~15% of IMAX Corp
profile: James E. Douglas III holds IMAX shares directly as part of a California family group reporting jointly with Kevin Douglas, the Douglas Family Trust, the James & Jean Douglas Irrevocable Descendants Trust, K&M Douglas Trust, Celtic Financial and the KGD 2012 Trust; Kevin Douglas holds dispositive power over his shares. The group has been a top IMAX holder since the mid-2000s; filings show he has been a Form 4 filer since 2007.
interesting_fact: The Douglas group he belongs to reported holding about 14.9% of IMAX in 2021, one of the largest stakes in the giant-screen company, and Kevin Douglas sits on IMAX's board.
notes: Essentially a passive family-investor name; no public profile, interviews or own channels. Filings do not spell out his exact relation to Kevin Douglas or to trustees James E. Douglas Jr. and Jean Douglas. Only published route is the Douglas family office in Larkspur, CA (early-warning-report contact Eileen Wheatman, per the newswire release) - best approached via Kevin Douglas/IMAX.

name: Liang Wanyun
current_role: Unknown; listed by Hurun China (2020-2021) as a wealth holder via Foshan Haitian Flavouring & Food (603288.SH / 3288.HK)
profile: Appeared on the Hurun China Rich List in 2020-2021 with a fortune tied to Haitian, China's largest soy-sauce and condiment maker, which was bought out by its employees in 2007 and whose shares are largely held via Guangdong Haitian Group. She does not appear among Haitian's top-10 shareholders in the 2020 or 2025 annual reports, and no public profile was found.
interesting_fact: Haitian traces its roots to a group of 17th-century Foshan sauce factories, was bought out from the Foshan government by its employees in 2007, and is the world's largest soy-sauce maker; it added a Hong Kong listing in 2025.
notes: Likely an indirect shareholder via Guangdong Haitian Group or a family member of a Haitian manager - unconfirmed. No public footprint; only route is Haitian board office.
